rating.sourceTitle: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde

longDescription: Atmosphere matters as much as action: unsettling places, uncertainty and emotional intensity shape the experience. Questions of trust, belonging and the limits of human understanding give the story resonance beyond its suspense. Read for the gradually deepening mood without needing to know its surprises in advance.

authorInfo.bio: Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish novelist, essayist, poet and travel writer. He is best known for the novels Treasure Island (1883), Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde (1886), and Kidnapped (1886) and for the poetry collection A Child's Garden of Verses (1885).
